name: Bánh bèo Cù Lao Chàm
summary: Bánh bèo is rice steamed in small cups, with a soft topping of shrimp, pork, and wood ear. The topping tastes of salty island fish sauce and sweet shrimp, and a brown sweet cake can sit beside it.
origin: Cham Islands. Steamed rice cakes on Tân Hiệp, ground with Cham well water.
texture: Ordinary rice, soaked and ground with Cham well water, steams in cups over a charcoal fire until a swirl shows in the middle. The topping of shrimp, pork, and wood-ear mushroom stays soft, not dry. A brown sweet cake is served in some stalls and is still eaten with the salty topping.
taste: The topping tastes of salty fish sauce made from island fish, and of sweet shrimp.
howToEat: A tray is 6 to 10 cups. The seller gives a small bamboo knife, not chopsticks and not a spoon. Cut the cake and spear a piece.
In the afternoon, with bánh xèo chả cá, bánh canh, and mì Quảng.
where: The Bai Lang coast road and the stalls by Giếng Xóm Cấm in Bai Ong.
seoTitle: Bánh bèo Cù Lao Chàm — steamed cups, bamboo knife
seoDescription: Small steamed rice cakes with a soft shrimp topping, salty and sweet, cut with a bamboo knife. Afternoon food on the Bai Lang coast road.
